1.w: And when He completed all His words in the hearing of the people, He entered into Capernaum.

2.w: And a certain servant of a centurion, who was valued highly to him, being ill, was about to die.

3.w: And having heard about Jesus, he sent elders of the Jews to Him, asking Him that, having come, He might save his servant.

4.w: And having come to Jesus, they were imploring Him earnestly, saying, “He is worthy to whom You will grant this,

5.w: for he loves our nation, and he built the synagogue for us.”

6.w: And Jesus was going with them, and now [in] His being not far away from the house, the centurion sent friends, saying to Him, “Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not fit that You should enter under my roof.

7.w: Therefore neither did I count myself worthy to come to You. But say a word, and let my servant be healed.

8.w: For I also am a man appointed under authority, having soldiers under me. And I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does.”

9.w: And having heard these things, Jesus marveled at him. And having turned to the crowd following Him, He said, “I say to you⁺, not even in Israel did I find such great faith.”

10.w: And having returned to the house, those having been sent found the servant in good health.

11.w: And it came to pass on the next day [that] He went into a city called Nain, and His disciples were going with Him, and a great crowd.

12.w: And as He drew near to the gate of the city, then, behold, a dead [man] was being carried out, the only begotten son of his mother; and she was a widow. And a large crowd of the city was with her.

13.w: And having seen her, the Lord was moved with compassion toward her and said to her, “Do not weep.”

14.w: And having come up, He touched the bier; and those bearing [it] stood still. And He said, “Young man, I say to you, arise!”

15.w: And the dead [man] sat up and began to speak, and He gave him to his mother.

16.w: And fear took all, and they were glorifying God, saying, “A great prophet arose among us!” and, “God visited His people!”

17.w: And the word of this went forth in all Judea about Him—and in all the surrounding region.

18.w: And his disciples reported to John about all these things.

19.w: And having summoned a certain two of his disciples, John sent to the Lord, saying, “Are You the coming One, or do we look for another?”

20.w: And having come to Him, the men said, “John the Baptist sent us to You, saying, ‘Are You the coming One, or do we look for another?’”

21.w: In that very hour, He healed many of diseases and afflictions and evil spirits, and to many blind He granted to see.

22.w: And answering, He said to them, “Having gone, report to John what you⁺ saw and heard: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news proclaimed.

23.w: And blessed is the one who shall not be caused to stumble in Me.”

24.w: And the messengers of John having gone away, He began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you⁺ go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?

25.w: But what did you⁺ go out to see? A man arrayed in soft garments? Behold, those in splendid clothing and living in luxury are in the palaces.

26.w: But what did you⁺ go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you⁺, and more than a prophet.

27.w: This is he about whom it has been written: ‘Behold, I send My messenger before Your face, who will prepare Your way before You.’

28.w: I say to you⁺, no one among [those] born of women is greater than John; yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”

29.w: And all the people having heard, even the tax collectors, declared God righteous, having been baptized [with] the baptism of John.

30.w: But the Pharisees and the lawyers set aside the counsel of God for themselves, not having been baptized by him.

31.w: “To what, therefore, will I liken the men of this generation? And to what are they like?

32.w: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling to one another, saying: ‘We played the flute for you⁺, and you⁺ did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you⁺ did not weep.’

33.w: For John the Baptist has come neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you⁺ say, ‘He has a demon!’

34.w: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you⁺ say, ‘Behold, a man, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and of sinners!’

35.w: And wisdom was justified from all her children.”

36.w: And one of the Pharisees was requesting of Him that He should eat with him, and having entered into the house of the Pharisee, He reclined.

37.w: And behold, a woman in the city who was a sinner. And having known that He is reclining in the house of the Pharisee, having taken an alabaster flask of fragrant oil,

38.w: and having stood behind [Him] at His feet weeping, she began to wet His feet with [her] tears, and she was wiping [them] with the hairs of her head, and she was kissing His feet and was anointing [them] with the fragrant oil.

39.w: And the Pharisee, the one having called Him, having seen, spoke within himself, saying, “If this [man] were a prophet, He would have known who and what kind the woman [is] who touches Him—because she is a sinner.”

40.w: And answering, Jesus said to him, “Simon, I have something to say to you.” And he says, “Teacher, say [it].”

41.w: “There were two debtors to a certain lender. The one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.

42.w: Of them having nothing to repay, he forgave both. Therefore which of them will love him more?”

43.w: Answering, Simon said, “I suppose [he] to whom he forgave the more.” And He said to him, “You judged correctly.”

44.w: And having turned to the woman, He was saying to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered into your house; you did not give water for My feet, but she herself wet My feet with [her] tears and wiped [them] with her hair.

45.w: You did not give to Me a kiss, but from which [time] I entered, she herself did not cease kissing My feet.

46.w: You did not anoint My head with oil, but she herself anointed My feet with fragrant oil.

47.w: Therefore I say to you this: Her many sins have been forgiven, because she loved much; but to whom little is forgiven, he loves little.”

48.w: And He said to her, “Your sins have been forgiven.”

49.w: And those reclining with [Him] began to say within themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”

50.w: And He said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
